statement: Economic-state equivalence between final and initial states does not imply preserved continuity.
A reconciled financial state does not imply preserved continuity.
Reconstructed continuity is distinct from uninterrupted preserved continuity.
Functional recovery is insufficient to establish continuity preservation.
Two histories may terminate in economically equivalent states while possessing different continuity classifications.
A history containing a qualifying continuity break cannot be classified PRESERVED for the complete interval.
PRESERVED and RECONSTRUCTED are mutually exclusive classifications for the same complete continuity interval.
A reconstructed continuity classification preserves evidence of the preceding continuity break.
Insufficient continuity evidence cannot be promoted to PRESERVED.
